title: Understanding Positional Embeddings in Modern LLMs
author: Sebastian Raschka, PhD
description: The Methods Behind How LLMs Represent Token Positions
summary: This article explains how LLMs encode and process token position information by covering classic and contemporary methods like RoPE. It’s essentially a comprehensive journey where we will work through the mechanisms with visual examples, a little math, and a small PyTorch implementation.
takeaways: The transformer blocks inside the LLM then modify these vectors using attention and feedforward layers.

As we can see, the architectures are not too different from each other, but before we get to the positional information parts, let’s focus on the orange blocks for now (the token embedding layers) and the transformer blocks above them; the other architecture differences aren’t needed for this explanation.
Note that this article assumes some familiarity with basic LLM architectures and works well as a follow-up to Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch) .
